SearchAliases: far side of Mighty Sound King
Senses.Explanation: Mighty-Sound King Buddha, a Buddha whom Zen records repeatedly invoke as an extreme before-and-after boundary. Huangbo Xiyun says he followed the Way before Mighty-Sound King; Nanquan Puyuan replies that Huangbo is still a descendant of old Master Wang, turning Nanquan's surname into the answer. Xuance says unaided self-awakening is acceptable before Mighty-Sound King but entirely the way of outsiders afterward. Xuedou Chongxian classifies unaided awakening before him as the second phrase. Tianyi Yihuai asks how many people Mighty-Sound King Buddha taught in his first assembly, then directs the audience to look at a ten-thousand-fathom peak. Dahui Zonggao critically reports people who call closed eyes news from the Buddha's far side. Hanyue Fazang describes paintings that place him before the seven buddhas as a circle preceding their differing verbal teachings, then gives a source-specific account of the name as outside form and sound and before writing. Juelang Daosheng asks whether his listeners have ever seen the power of Mighty-Sound King Buddha. The Zen figure is thus defined by these deployments: a named limit in lineage claims, interview questions, classification, painting, and criticism, not by a detached hagiography.

Occurrences.Kwic: 檗曰。威音王已前。師曰。猶是王老師兒孫在。下去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): Huangbo Xiyun says "before Mighty-Sound King"; Nanquan Puyuan replies that Huangbo is still old Master Wang's descendant.

Occurrences.Kwic: 威音王已前即得，威音王已後無師自悟，盡是天然外道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Linked Lamps (聯燈會要): Xuance tells Yongjia Xuanjue that unaided self-awakening is acceptable before Mighty-Sound King but entirely the way of outsiders afterward.

Occurrences.Kwic: 閉眉合眼。謂之威音王那畔父母未生時消息。亦謂之默而常照。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited recorded-sayings collection (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao critically reports people who close their eyes and call that news from the far side of Mighty-Sound King and before their parents were born.

Occurrences.Kwic: 威音王已前無師自悟。是第二句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited recorded-sayings collection (明覺禪師語錄): Xuedou Chongxian says that unaided self-awakening before Mighty-Sound King is the second phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臨濟宗嘗見繪事家圖，七佛之始，始于威音王佛。惟大作一○圓相之後，則七佛各有言詮。言詮雖異，而諸佛之偈旨不出圓相也。夫威者，形之外者也。音者，聲之外者也。威音王者，形聲之外，未有出載，無所考據，文字以前最上事也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited recorded-sayings collection (三峰藏和尚語錄): Hanyue Fazang describes paintings that put Mighty-Sound King Buddha first as a circle before the seven buddhas' verbal teachings, then offers his source-specific account of the name as outside form and sound and before writing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只如威音王佛最初一會度多少人？若是通方作者，試為道看。良久，云：行路難，行路難，萬仞峰前著眼看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Linked Lamps (聯燈會要): Tianyi Yihuai asks how many people Mighty-Sound King Buddha taught at his first assembly, waits, and tells the audience to look carefully at the ten-thousand-fathom peak.

Occurrences.Kwic: 還曾見有威音王佛與日月燈明佛底神力者麼？若論遮箇，誰不能知？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited complete recorded-sayings collection (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄): Juelang Daosheng asks whether his listeners have ever seen the power of Mighty-Sound King Buddha and Sun-Moon-Lamp-Light Buddha.
